# transforms.library: Offset

**Status:** Supported (tier `foundation`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_OriginPlusOffsetRecoversPosition2D

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 154](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L154)

```plato
// A position is its origin displaced by its own offset. This is the IOriginBased
// round trip, and it is what makes Offset/FromOffset a genuine isomorphism rather
// than two unrelated conversions.
Law_OriginPlusOffsetRecoversPosition2D(p: Point2D): Boolean
    => p.Origin.Add(p.Offset).Distance(p) <= 1e-4;
```

### Law_OriginPlusOffsetRecoversPosition3D

```plato
Law_OriginPlusOffsetRecoversPosition3D(p: Point3D): Boolean
    => p.Origin.Add(p.Offset).Distance(p) <= 1e-4;
```

### Law_OriginIsEpoch

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 162](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L162)

```plato
// The epoch is the origin: an Instant's offset from the origin is its own
// seconds-since-epoch. Ties the derived Origin back to the field it came from.
Law_OriginIsEpoch(t: Instant): Boolean
    => t.Origin.Add(t.Offset).SecondsSinceEpoch.LawEq(t.SecondsSinceEpoch);
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Point support
    //
    // The IDifference obligations of Point2D/Point3D, point interpolation, and the
    // explicit point <-> vector converters that every other transform library builds
    // on. Kept separate from the representations because nothing here depends on a
    // transform type.

    //==
    // Point support — the IOriginBased conversions of Point2D/Point3D/PointN, and
    // the explicit point <-> vector converters spelled in the direction callers
    // read them.
    //
    // NOTHING else is written here. Add, Between, Subtract (both spellings) and
    // Lerp are all derived from Offset and FromOffset via algebra.library.plato.
    // The converters remain deliberately named
    // rather than implicit conversions: silently coercing between positions and
    // displacements would defeat the point of keeping them distinct types.

    // The point's displacement from the origin.
    Offset(p: Point2D): Vector2D
        => (p.X, p.Y);
```

```plato
    // The point's displacement from the origin. Arity is carried by the
    // component array, so no separate arity argument is needed.
    // Written as an explicit construction, not a parenthesized value: the single field is an
    // Array, and a C# backend cannot declare the implicit conversion for an interface-typed
    // field (CS0552), so the structural form has nothing to convert through.
    Offset(p: PointN): VectorN
        => VectorN(p.Components);
```
